title: A .camtools library cannot hold a form-profile mill, a blunt tapered mill, or a single-form thread mill without a pitch range

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
CamCraft at c5bb09ed13f8b63e691d3a5ed6fb0be6a64ee2aa.

## What other tool libraries store

Fusion tool libraries store three kinds of mill that a `camcraft-tools` definition has no field for:

1. Form mill: a drawn profile, a list of (radius, height) points from the axis at the tip, round the cutter and back to the axis. It covers thread mills, double-angle cutters, radius-profile cutters and any ground shape.
2. Tapered mill: a cone with a tip diameter (flat) or a corner radius (ball) at the tip, a taper angle per side and a shoulder diameter at the cutting length (tapered engravers, ball-tip tapered mills).
3. Single-form thread mill: one tooth in the profile; Fusion states no pitch range (the range is in the description text, if anywhere).

## What is missing

- `kind: taper` is a cone from a sharp apex. A tool with a tip diameter or a ball tip has no field; writing it as `taper` shifts the cone by half the tip diameter at every height.
- The drawn cutter outline (`set_tool_cutter_profile`, `ToolCutter`) exists in a project but a `.camtools` definition cannot carry it (`tool_edit` lists `cutter` as not here), so an arbitrary form profile cannot travel with the tool. `kind: form` is a lathe gauge.
- `thread_mill_single` needs `pitch` and `pitch_min`; a source that stores only the tooth has neither.
- Smaller: the dovetail check `top < sr` compares with no tolerance, so a neck that meets the flank exactly (head 6.096 mm, 1.4605 mm high, 45 degree flank, neck 3.175 mm) is refused by float dust: `3.048 - 1.4605 / tan(45 deg)` is one ulp under `1.5875`.

## Synthetic example

Form mill, mm: profile `(0,0) (2,0) (4,0.8) (2,1.6) (2,9) (4,11) (4,40) (0,40)` (one 43.6 degree V tooth on a 4 mm radius shank).
Tapered mill, mm: tip diameter 1, taper angle 30 degrees per side, cutting length 10, shoulder diameter 12.

## Ask

Any of: a `tip_d` (and ball radius) on `taper`; an optional `cutter` outline in the definition, judged by `cutter_profile::check`; an optional `pitch_min` default for `thread_mill_single`; a small tolerance in the dovetail neck check.

Until then Dutchman writes only the multi-form thread mill (rows of equal teeth at one pitch, read from the profile) and the sharp-tipped taper, and reports the others as not carried over.

## Measured

On a 97-tool Fusion library: 85 written, 12 not written (11 single-tooth form mills, 1 tapered mill with a ball tip). One multi-form thread mill and one dovetail now convert.
